BATCH A APPROVED as one batch — every FIX recommendation of rebuild/m2/AUDIT-REGISTER.md becomes an approved repair direction: D1 APPROVED-FIX · D2 APPROVED-FIX · D3 APPROVED-FIX · D4 APPROVED-FIX · D5 APPROVED-FIX · D6 APPROVED-FIX · D7 APPROVED-FIX · D9 APPROVED-FIX · D11 APPROVED-FIX · D12 APPROVED-FIX · D13 APPROVED-FIX · D14 APPROVED-FIX · D15 APPROVED-FIX · D17 APPROVED-FIX · D18 APPROVED-FIX · D19 APPROVED-FIX · D20 APPROVED-FIX · D21 APPROVED-FIX · D22 APPROVED-FIX · D23 APPROVED-FIX · D24 APPROVED-FIX · D26 APPROVED-FIX · D27 APPROVED-FIX · D28 APPROVED-FIX · D29 APPROVED-FIX · D30 APPROVED-FIX · D31 APPROVED-FIX · D33 APPROVED-FIX · D34 APPROVED-FIX · D35 APPROVED-FIX · D36 APPROVED-FIX · D38 APPROVED-FIX · D39 APPROVED-FIX · D41 APPROVED-FIX · D42 APPROVED-FIX · D43 APPROVED-FIX · D44 APPROVED-FIX · D45 APPROVED-FIX (38). BATCH B — all seven RECOMMENDED answers chosen, each now an approved repair direction with its exact rule: D8 APPROVED-FIX — when last night's sleep is missing, recovery is UNKNOWN and no sleep restriction is applied today; every other recovery check still applies (not carry-forward of the last logged night). D10 APPROVED-FIX — date-only week counts mean 7 CALENDAR days, not 168 elapsed hours. D16 APPROVED-FIX — a 7-day forecast hit requires an eligible weigh-in on the due day or, failing that, the next day (one grace date); with no such reading the forecast is UNGRADED, not a miss; the day arithmetic follows D10. D25 APPROVED-FIX — "protein: good" requires at least one successful day within the current seven-logged-days window before the one-miss allowance applies; a first missed day cannot read "good". D32 APPROVED-FIX — "benefit replicated" counts only sessions from the CURRENT technique; all other replication thresholds stay as they are. D37 APPROVED-FIX — a merged earned receipt keeps the assessment as of the day it was earned, accepting that this can change whether a single-sighting increase counts as earned and the numbers printed on past earned receipts. D40 APPROVED-FIX — when two phones disagree on a day's calories with equal detail, ONE deterministic shared winner is chosen with the conflict kept visible and BOTH original entries retained; the exact tie-break rule and how the conflict is shown are NOT decided here and must be specified in the reviewed fix brief before anything is built. Totals: 45/45 dispositions recorded, 45 APPROVED-FIX, 0 KEEP, 0 DEFER, 0 UNRULED. What this does NOT do: it approves directions, not code — each theme still needs its accepted behaviour/delta brief, its red-first laws turning GREEN on the candidate and RED on the frozen engine, the post-fix gate's PACKAGE run and cowork's execution acceptance; the frozen app and its goldens stay untouched; no private release, spending, phone gate, remote gate or M2 closure is waived; no owner-specific interval or value is set. Transport: the route ruling at line 42 applies; no additional Go was requested or given · rebuild/m2/OWNER-RULING-PACK-M2.md · M2-RULE DONE; M2-FIX unblocked for briefs (D33–D35 first, per the accepted PR #34 contract)

notes: SKELETON, AUTHORED BY THE TOOLING FIXER, NOT BY THE PACKAGE. DECISIONS:124 created M2-H3-CLEAN-INIT on 2026-09-12; this file exists so the runner admits the id and so the chain’s shape is visible. It makes NO claim about the clean-init defect, its scope or its evidence. The package itself — brief, product post-images, D-id/register accounting, children, coverage — is authored by its own builder.

H3 IS A NO-REGISTER PACKAGE, and the runner now says so. TOOLING-REVIEW r7 item 2 wrote the rule down in the runner beside NO_REGISTER_IDS itself: every H-/F- item is an ENGINE-TIER register item that carries no D-id (DECISIONS:93 — feature work under the ratified slice plan takes no register D-ID), and a B- package is exempt only where the PM ruled it so by name (DECISIONS:103 (1) for B-NTC and B-LOM). DECISIONS:124 rules M2-H3-CLEAN-INIT an engine-tier item beside H1/H2 and names no D-id for it, so H3 enters under the H- half of the rule and not by anybody's discretion. The earlier note here said every run of H3 refused at REGISTER-D-ID-INVENTORY-EMPTY-AND-NOT-EXEMPT; it no longer does. What H3 now owes instead is Y1's replacement obligation — at least MIN_OWN_CHILDREN declared child(ren) executing one of its own role:"new" product files — which is OPEN on every run until its own builder declares them, and refuses at the seal.

product declares exactly the one file DECISIONS:124 names in scope — rebuild/m4/workout/athlete-state.cjs, role "edited" — with its pre-image taken from the bytes standing here now and post null, because the post-image does not exist yet. Role "edited" is the truth of what :124 rules (createCleanInitState gains blackout and the model members bfEst reads); it is not a claim that any of it is written. TOOLING-REVIEW r7 F5 asked whether this shape survives the new product rules: it does, and for the reason the role gives — pre is a real sha and post is null, so pre !== post and the r7 F1 refusal PRODUCT-CHANGE-ROLE-DECLARES-NO-CHANGE cannot fire on it. The role that WOULD refuse here is "new" with pre === post; a file this package declares, runs and leaves alone is role "pinned-unchanged", and a file it edits states a post it does not already stand at.

parent is UNDECIDED: H3’s only parent option is the B-NTC artifact, which is not sealed. DECISIONS:116 (3) has the lane rehearse H3 against the B-NTC candidate head, so only pins move after B-NTC seals — and pins are exactly what this file does not take.
